item.title: Morgan Stanley Sees Pressure Rising on Chipmakers’ Pricing Power
item.description: Morgan Stanley’s Lisa Shalett urged investors to be cautious on chipmakers as evidence mounts that their pricing power is limited, suggesting that the stocks may have rallied too far on optimism around artificial-intelligence spending.

item.title: La dette cachée freine le développement du Sénégal: Next Africa
item.description: Les grands projets d’infrastructure devaient incarner la transformation du Sénégal en l’une des économies les plus dynamiques d’Afrique de l’Ouest.

item.title: SK Hynix Indicated to Climb 21% After $26.5 Billion ADR Offering
item.description: SK Hynix Inc.’s American depositary receipts are indicated to open 21% above their offering price, after the South Korean memory chipmaker raised $26.5 billion in the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company.

item.title: Prediction Market Bets Surge on World Cup Mania
item.description: Rabid interest in the World Cup has helped to drive more than $3 billion of wagers on a prediction market backed by Robinhood Markets Inc. and Susquehanna International Group, which launched just a few months ago.

item.title: Retail Traders Chase Shiny Objects But Refuse to Bet on S&P 500
item.description: Retail traders, some of the staunchest supporters of the stock market this decade, are showing signs of waning conviction.

item.title: AlphaQuest Founder Lost Control at Quant Fund, Investor Alleges
item.description: AlphaQuest founder Nigol Koulajian admitted losing control of trading at his $2 billion quantitative hedge fund before announcing plans to shut it down, an institutional investor claimed in a lawsuit.

item.title: Macro Hedge Fund Deem Raised $1 Billion From Abu Dhabi’s ADIC
item.description: Asfandyar Nadeem’s hedge fund has received about $1 billion in new capital from an Abu Dhabi investor, amid a surge in appetite for macro strategies and as the Gulf city accelerates its drive to become a key backer of the industry.

item.title: Raytheon, Rheinmetall Anchor AI Training Effort for UK Army
item.description: The UK Ministry of Defense awarded a £2 billion ($2.7 billion) contract for AI-based military training to a Raytheon-led consortium that includes European defense prime Rheinmetall AG.

item.title: Czech Price Pressures Warrant Increased Caution for Central Bank
item.description: The Czech central bank said monetary policy caution remains warranted, with the headline inflation rate likely to return to or “slightly above” the 2% target this year following a recent drop.

item.title: Canada Adds 18,200 Jobs in June as Young Workers Catch a Break
item.description: Employment in Canada rose 18,200 in June and the unemployment rate fell to 6.5% as the country’s labor market shows some signs of tightening.

item.title: Brazil Inflation Surprise Bolsters Case for More Rate Cuts
item.description: Brazil’s annual inflation unexpectedly slowed in June, offering some relief to policymakers after the central bank delivered its third consecutive interest-rate cut even as price growth remained above target.

item.title: Shein Gets Approval From Chinese Regulator for Hong Kong IPO
item.description: Shein Global Holdings Ltd. got approval from the Chinese regulator to move ahead with its planned initial public offering in Hong Kong, capping a yearslong effort by the fast-fashion giant to go public.

item.title: Oil Product Markets Are the Real Hormuz Pain Point
item.description: While crude has nearly erased its wartime rally, refined fuels are increasingly tight.

item.title: Novogratz Morphs Galaxy Into AI Landlord, One Gigawatt at a Time
item.description: Mike Novogratz joked he might be ready for another tattoo.

item.title: Echostar Bulls Say It Offers Traders Discounted SpaceX Exposure
item.description: SpaceX may finally be within reach for public-market investors, but analysts say there’s a cheaper opportunity to get exposure to shares of the space technology company through EchoStar Corp.

item.title: Foreign Ownership of UK Firms Soared 35% Amid Glut of Deals
item.description: The number of British companies controlled by overseas firms soared 35% in the years after the outbreak of Covid, as cheap valuations drove a dealmaking boom.

item.title: US Stock Futures Slip After Tech Rally, SK Hynix Starts Trading
item.description: US equities were moving between losses and gains Friday as investors digested the record US listing of South Korea’s SK Hynix Inc. and prepared for the start of second-quarter earnings season.

item.title: SMFG Said to Weigh Strategy for India Assets Including Yes Bank
item.description: Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group Inc. is evaluating its India strategy as it looks for ways to consolidate its presence in one of the world’s fastest-growing banking markets, people with knowledge of the matter said.

item.title: SK Hynix Is Making History With Its US Debut
item.description: The memory chipmaker represents a pure-play bet on the AI boom

item.title: ‘Ziplink Is Now Froggle’: The Story Behind the Fake AI Ads That Went Viral
item.description: The surge in tech campaigns on public transit is spurring satirists from New York to London to create their own versions.

item.title: AI Is Driving a Wave of Business Formations in the US
item.description: Projections of new firms within the coming year soared to a record in some sectors

item.title: A Month After SpaceX IPO, Tesla’s Stock Keeps Holding Its Ground
item.description: In the weeks leading up to SpaceX’s monster IPO, many Wall Street pros feared the deal represented an existential threat for Elon Musk’s other giant, Tesla Inc. But after a month in the stock market, the outcome is far from clear.

item.title: China Vanke Says First-Half Loss May Widen to $2.2 Billion
item.description: China Vanke Co. said its first-half loss could reach $2.2 billion due to low gross margins on property development projects and asset impairment charges.

item.title: Kenya First-Quarter Growth Rebounds as Agriculture Recovers
item.description: Kenya’s economy picked up steam in the first quarter, underpinned by a general improvement in performance across board and a rebound in agriculture.

item.title: Sovereign AI May Mean State-Backed Models and Political Tensions
item.description: Washington wants in on the artificial intelligence gold rush.

item.title: Big Tech Doubles Debt Load to $350 Billion in AI Spending Spree
item.description: The largest builders of artificial intelligence data centers have doubled their debt load in the last five years, turning to borrowing to finance an unprecedented spending spree they claim is needed to transform the economy.

item.title: Milky Mist Said to Launch $213 Million India IPO This Month
item.description: Milky Mist Dairy Food Ltd. is gearing up to launch its 20.35 billion rupees ($213 million) initial public offering as early as July, according to people familiar with the matter, paving the way for what is expected to be India’s largest dairy-sector IPO.

item.title: Traders Hedge for FX Volatility Return as Fed Uncertainty Builds
item.description: Currency traders are starting to buy protection against bigger exchange-rate swings after months of calm, as banks warn that shifting Federal Reserve expectations and elevated geopolitical tensions could be about to jolt markets.

item.title: South Africa’s Absa Faces Deeper Slide as Analysts Turn Cautious
item.description: A selloff in Absa Group Ltd. shares may have further to run as the South African lender’s disappointing earnings guidance causes once-bullish analysts to turn cautious on the stock.

item.title: Pfizer Vaccine Dispute Hits Polish, Romania Air Traffic Agencies
item.description: Poland and Romania’s legal battles with Pfizer Inc. over unused Covid-19 vaccine purchases are spilling into the funding of the eastern European nations’ air traffic agencies.
